t.6.96.1: All beings beheld those two, Rāma and Rāvaṇa, fighting thus in battle, with their inmost hearts filled with wonder.
t.6.96.2: Assailing in battle those two excellent chariots of theirs, the two warriors, bent on slaying each other, became terrible to behold.
t.6.96.3: The two charioteers displayed circling movements and straight runs, advances and retreats, the many kinds of motion that spring from the art of charioteering.
t.6.96.5: As the two of them hurled nets of arrows, those two excellent chariots of theirs ranged over the battlefield like two clouds pouring down showers of rain.
t.6.96.4: Rāma harassed Rāvaṇa, and Rāvaṇa too harassed Rāghava; the two of them attained great swiftness of motion in advancing and retreating.
t.6.96.6: Then the two of them, having displayed many kinds of movement in battle, stood once again facing each other.
t.6.96.7: Then, as the two chariots stood there, pole met pole, the faces of the horses met face to face, and banners came together with banners.
t.6.96.8: Then Rāma, with four sharp arrows loosed from his bow, drove back the four blazing horses of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.96.10: Though deeply pierced by the mighty Daśagrīva, Rāghava did not waver, nor was he pained in the least.
t.6.96.9: When his horses fell back, that night-rover, overcome by fury, loosed sharp arrows at Rāghava.
t.6.96.11: And again the night-roamer hurled arrows whose sound was like the crash of a thunderbolt, aiming at the charioteer of the thunderbolt-wielder.
t.6.96.12: But the arrows of great speed that fell upon Mātali's body in the battle caused him not even the slightest bewilderment or pain.
t.6.96.13: Enraged by that assault upon Mātali, and not so much by the one upon himself, Rāghava with a net of arrows made his enemy turn his face away.
t.6.96.14: The heroic Rāghava loosed arrows upon his enemy's chariot, twenty, thirty, sixty, then by hundreds and by thousands.
t.6.96.15: By the clangor of maces, pestles and iron bars, and by the rush of wind from the feathered ends of arrows, the seven oceans were stirred into turmoil.
t.6.96.16: As the oceans were churned into turmoil, all the serpents dwelling in the depths of Pātāla, and the Dānavas in their thousands, were stricken with distress.
t.6.96.17: The whole earth, with its mountains, woods and forests, trembled; the sun became lustreless, and the wind ceased to blow.
t.6.96.18: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the supreme sages, all of them together with the Kiṃnaras and great serpents, fell into anxious thought.
t.6.96.19: May there be well-being for cows and brāhmaṇas, may the worlds endure forever; may Rāghava conquer in battle Rāvaṇa, the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.96.20: Then the mighty-armed Rāma, enhancer of the glory of the Raghus, enraged, fixed on his bow a razor-edged arrow like a venomous serpent and cut off Rāvaṇa's splendid head with its blazing earrings.
t.6.96.21: That head, fallen upon the ground, was then seen by the three worlds; and another head of Rāvaṇa, just like it, rose up in its place.
t.6.96.22: Swiftly, in the battle, that second head of Rāvaṇa too was severed with arrows by Rāma, swift of hand and swift in action.
t.6.96.23: And no sooner was that head cut off than another head was seen once more; that too was cut off by Rāma with arrows resembling thunderbolts.
t.6.96.24: In just this way a hundred heads of equal splendor have been cut off, and yet no end of Rāvaṇa, no destruction of his life, is to be seen.
t.6.96.25: Then Rāghava, the hero versed in all weapons, who increased the joy of Kausalyā, furnished with many arrows, fell to thinking.
t.6.96.27: These are all those arrows of mine that have proved trustworthy in battle; what then is the reason by which they have become feeble in their power against Rāvaṇa?
t.6.96.26: Those by whom Mārīca was slain, by whom Khara and the dreadful Dūṣaṇa were struck down, by whom Virādha was killed in the Krauñca forest and Kabandha in the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.6.96.28: Thus he became absorbed in thought, yet remained ever vigilant in the battle; and Rāghava rained down showers of arrows upon the chest of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.96.29: Then Rāvaṇa too, the lord of the rākṣasas, enraged and standing in his chariot, struck back at Rāma in battle with a shower of maces and pestles.
t.6.96.30: While the Devas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Piśācas, Uragas and Rākṣasas looked on, that great battle went on all night long.
t.6.96.31: Neither by night nor by day, not for a muhūrta nor even for a moment, did the battle between Rāma and Rāvaṇa come to a pause.
